governed_construct: One read of the device/system colour scheme for dark-mode support: a call to any function named or aliased as useColorScheme (whatever it is bound to), a call to Appearance.getColorScheme or Appearance.addChangeListener, or a matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: ...)') query.
interpretation: Expo's useColorScheme is the useColorScheme hook that Expo exposes from 'react-native'. An instance conforms when the colour scheme is obtained through a call that resolves to that hook: a named import from 'react-native' (including aliased imports), a namespace import (RN.useColorScheme()), or a local wrapper whose body itself delegates to the react-native hook. An instance does not conform when the scheme comes from anywhere else: Appearance.getColorScheme()/addChangeListener read imperatively, window.matchMedia on prefers-color-scheme, or a same-named useColorScheme hook from another package (nativewind, react-native-appearance). The verdict follows the binding of the identifier that is actually called, not the presence of an import or of the name; a react-native import that is only used in a type position is not an instance. A file with any non-conforming scheme read is VIOLATED even if it also uses the react-native hook. A file that reads no colour scheme at all is NOT_APPLICABLE.
